question: Who is known as the father of Indian Census?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Walter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Henry Walter** is regarded as the "Father of the Indian Census" for organizing the first modern census in India in 1830.
 
• The first systematic census in India was conducted under British rule by Henry Walter in the town of Dacca (now Dhaka) in 1830.
 
• Henry Walter was instrumental in introducing the concept of recording population statistics in an organized and structured manner.
 
• This laid the foundation for the decennial census system in India, which officially began in 1872 and continues to this day.
 
• The census in India now provides critical data for planning and policy-making, a practice rooted in the groundwork laid by Henry Walter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Census Overview:**

 
 
• The Indian Census is conducted every 10 years, providing detailed demographic, social, and economic data.
 
• The first official synchronous census in India was conducted in 1881 under British rule.
 
• Post-independence, the Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
 
 
• **Decennial Census:**
 
 
• The census collects data on population, literacy, occupation, religion, language, and housing, among other parameters.
 
• The data is vital for planning welfare schemes, resource allocation, and policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Census:**
 
 
• It helps in understanding the demographic changes and trends over time.
 
• The census data is crucial for electoral delimitation and the allocation of parliamentary seats.
 
• It supports the government in addressing socio-economic issues effectively.
 
 
 
• **Modern Census Techniques:**
 
 
• The 2021 Census aimed to leverage digital technologies for faster and more accurate data collection.
 
• For the first time, citizens were given the option of self-enumeration through a mobile app.
